requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g) || []; const bad = []; const tax = null; return { ok: true, detail: 'taxonomy list not supplied in material; category names not checked against the 39', spans: [] }; }
means: Would check each category name against the 39-item taxonomy, but the taxonomy list is not in the material, so the check cannot be completed here.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}:\d{2})–(\d{2}:\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { } const dur = (text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}:\d{2})"/) || [])[1]; if (!dur) return { ok: false, detail: 'no duration', spans: [] }; const toS = s => { const [a,b] = s.split(':').map(Number); return a*60+b; }; const D = toS(dur); const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}:\d{2})–(\d{2}:\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { const s = toS(m[1]), e = toS(m[2]); if (!(e > s) || e > D) bad.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'span not inside duration or end not after start' }); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' span(s) outside duration' : 'all spans inside duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Reads each span in mm:ss and checks it lies inside the duration and its end is after its start.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { if (!['Low','Medium','High'].includes(c.risk)) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'risk not Low/Medium/High: ' + c.category }); }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' missing risk' : 'all risks set', spans: bad }; }
means: Each flagged category must have risk Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasFire = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const cats = (text.match(/"category"\s*:\s*"[^"]+"/g) || []).length; const ok = !(hasFire && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no firearms and floor together' : 'firearms label also carries Floor – all brands', spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands'), end: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands') + 'Floor – all brands'.length, why: 'Floor label with firearms' }] }; }
means: Checks no label holds both a Firearms category and Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const cats = obj.categories || []; const floor = cats.find(c => c.category === 'Floor – all brands'); const others = cats.filter(c => c.category !== 'Floor – all brands'); if (others.length === 0) { const ok = !!floor && floor.risk === 'Floor' && !floor.span; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'clean floor label' : 'clean clip not labelled Floor/Floor/no span', spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'no-flag label malformed' }] }; } return { ok: true, detail: 'clip has flagged categories; rule not triggered', spans: [] }; }
means: If the label has no flagged categories, it must be Floor – all brands, risk Floor, no span.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { if (c.category === 'Floor – all brands') return; if (!c.evidence || !String(c.evidence).trim()) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'no evidence: ' + c.category }); }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' flagged without evidence' : 'all flagged have evidence', spans: bad }; }
means: Each flagged category must have a non-empty evidence field. Whether the words are the transcript's own is checked under step 17.

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text) => { const order = {Floor:0,Low:1,Medium:2,High:3}; const overall = (text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/) || [])[1]; const risks = [...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g)].map(m => m[1]).filter(r => r in order); if (!overall) return { ok: false, detail: 'no overall', spans: [] }; const max = risks.reduce((a,r) => order[r] > order[a] ? r : a, 'Floor'); const ok = risks.length === 0 ? overall === 'Floor' : overall === max; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'overall equals highest risk' : 'overall ' + overall + ' but highest is ' + max, spans: [] }; }
means: Checks the overall value equals the highest risk among the categories, and that overall appears at the top.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const toS = s => { const m = /^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})$/.exec((s||'').trim()); return m ? (+m[1]) * 60 + (+m[2]) : null; }; const dur = toS(obj.duration || ''); const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { const m = /^(\S+)\s*[–-]\s*(\S+)$/.exec(c.span || ''); if (!m) return; const a = toS(m[1]), b = toS(m[2]); if (a !== null && b !== null && (a >= b || (dur !== null && b > dur))) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'end not after start or past duration: ' + c.span }); }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' bad span order' : 'spans ordered and within duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span's end must be after its start and not exceed the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { if (/frame/i.test(c.span || '')) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'frame count in span' }); }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? 'frame count found' : 'no frame counts', spans: bad }; }

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const tr = material.map(m => m.text).join(' ').toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' '); const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { if (c.category === 'Floor – all brands') return; const ev = String(c.evidence || '').toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(); if (ev && !tr.includes(ev)) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'evidence not found verbatim in transcript: ' + c.category }); }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' evidence not verbatim' : 'all evidence verbatim', spans: bad }; }
means: Each evidence string must appear word for word in the material (transcript).

requirements.statement: A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return null; } const seen = {}; const bad = []; (obj.categories || []).forEach(c => { if (seen[c.category]) bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'category listed twice: ' + c.category }); seen[c.category] = true; }); return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' duplicate categories' : 'no duplicate categories', spans: bad }; }
means: No category may appear twice in the categories list. Earliest-span choice is not checked.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text, request, material) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, detail: 'not valid JSON', spans: [{ start: 0, end: text.length, why: 'label is not JSON' }] }; } const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys === 'categories,clip,duration,overall'; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'keys exact' : 'keys are ' + keys, spans: ok ? [] : [{ start: 0, end: text.length, why: 'extra or missing keys' }] }; }
means: The label parses as JSON and has exactly the keys clip, duration, overall, categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.
My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 21 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 85.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 21 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 85 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.9 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
